problem: 'gains happiness and riches' makes the roar the one who gains (अर्जनं सुखसम्पदाम् = the winning of happiness and riches for the chanter); and 'The roar of Rāma, Rāma' reads as Rāma's own roar, not the chanting of the name. Verse order (भर्जन, अर्जन, तर्जन … गर्जन) can be kept.
fix: Roasting the seeds of worldly existence, winning happiness and riches, threatening the messengers of Yama: such is the roar of the name Rāma, Rāma.

problem: पुरुषः (sh22) and पुराणपुरुषोत्तमः (sh23) are separate names among the sixteen, but both come out as 'Supreme Person' in English, so a reader cannot tell them apart; 'Supreme' is also not in पुरुषः. Hindi (परम पुरुष / पुरातन पुरुषोत्तम) keeps them apart and can stay.
fix: Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, the valiant, he whom Lakṣmaṇa follows, the mighty; the descendant of Kakutstha, the Puruṣa, the Perfect One, the son of Kausalyā, the best of the Raghus;

problem: 'Whatever virtuous person' is unnatural English, and 'endowed with the strength of Rāma' after 'Rakṣā' can be read as describing the person.
fix: The virtuous person who recites this Rakṣā, which carries the strength of Rāma, becomes long-lived, happy, blessed with sons, victorious and humble.

problem: 'Remembering him' has no antecedent when the verse is read on its own (sh11 speaks only of the names); the verse has no pronoun, only the names marked by इति. Hindi has no pronoun either.
fix: Remembering the name Rāma, Rāmabhadra or Rāmacandra, a person stays unstained by sin, and obtains both the pleasures of this world and liberation.

problem: The series 'self-controlled, ascetics and celibate' mixes a noun into a row of adjectives.
fix: They live on fruits and roots; they are self-controlled, ascetic and celibate. These two are the sons of Daśaratha, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.

problem: 'the deity is Śrī Sītā and Rāmacandra' joins two names to a singular verb; the Sanskrit is one compound deity (श्रीसीतारामचन्द्रो देवता), as the Hindi श्रीसीतारामचन्द्रजी shows.
fix: Of this mantra, the Śrī Rāma Rakṣā Stotra: the seer is Budha Kauśika; the deity is Śrī Sītā with Rāmacandra; the metre is anuṣṭubh; its power is Sītā; its kīlaka (the pin that holds the mantra fast) is the glorious Hanumān; and it is applied in the recitation of the Rāma Rakṣā Stotra, for the pleasure of Śrī Rāmacandra.

problem: करुणाकरं rendered 'a mine of mercy': the style sheet keeps करुणा = compassion (दया = mercy), and sh26 करुणार्णवं is 'ocean of compassion'. The verse itself repeats the word (कारुण्य-, करुणा-).
fix: The delight of the world, steadfast on the field of battle, lotus-eyed, lord of the line of Raghu, compassion in person and a mine of compassion: I take refuge in that Śrī Rāmacandra.

problem: जाम्बवान्‌के: the style table has जाम्बवान्‌जी (honorific), as the batch already does for विश्वामित्रजी, भरतजी, परशुरामजी, हनुमान्‌जी.
fix: सीतापति मेरे हाथोंकी रक्षा करें, जमदग्निनन्दन परशुरामजीको जीतनेवाले मेरे हृदयकी; खरका संहार करनेवाले मेरे शरीरके मध्यभागकी रक्षा करें, और जाम्बवान्‌जीके आश्रय मेरी नाभिकी।

problem: राम और लक्ष्मण without honorifics, while sh2, sh5, sh21, sh22, sh26, sh31 have लक्ष्मणजी and the batch uses श्रीराम for रामः (style §4: honorific for Lakṣmaṇa).
fix: वे फल और मूल खाते हैं, संयमी, तपस्वी और ब्रह्मचारी हैं; ये दोनों दशरथके पुत्र, भाई श्रीराम और लक्ष्मणजी हैं।

problem: राम और लक्ष्मण without honorifics; sh21, the next verse, has श्रीराम … लक्ष्मणजीके साथ.
fix: चढ़ी हुई प्रत्यंचावाले धनुष लिये, बाणोंको छूते हुए और अक्षय बाणोंसे भरे तरकस धारण किये श्रीराम और लक्ष्मणजी मेरी रक्षाके लिये सदा ही मार्गमें मेरे आगे चलें।

problem: Writer's word issue for मनोरमे adds a vocative sense ('हे मनोरमे') that our meaning does not use; §11 lists the senses the work uses. Not needed unless the owner chooses the vocative reading in the doubt.
fix: मनोरमे: मनको रमानेवाले (राम)में | in the heart-delighting one (unchanged)
